assessments.reasoning: The Index's own decision at commit d305c6ff9c1711877265b61cf44bfc1e0c09370b is primary evidence of its editorial assignment. The complete 1,997-byte capture contains the row for 1a07620194554b8db89bfcbfc70c3e05, edition lppl-1-3c-publisher-reference, the claimed SHA-256, and identifier LPPL-1.3c. The neighboring editions have distinct identifiers and digests. The closing qualification limits publication status.

The SPDX repository's GitHub API returned the complete annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b. Its tag is v3.29.0 and its target is a commit with the exact SHA used by the details URL. The API reports an unsigned tag, so the release binding rests on repository provenance and the inspected object fields. The detail record supplies the separate evidence of membership.

The LaTeX Project's edition-specific HTTPS plaintext names the LaTeX3 Project. Both contiguous partitions cover all 19,036 bytes and report SHA-256 c1ae6e179a6d28bbd5c483fbacc744acc75e922d598281dc3390aab26126e163, matching the Index row. Part 1 supplies the 1.3c heading and date. Part 2 supplies the example notice and nonreplacement paragraph. The example's dates describe the example and distribution, preserving the distinct meaning of the heading date.

The SPDX repository serves json/details/LPPL-1.3c.json at the tag's target commit. Six contiguous partitions cover all 84,386 bytes and report SHA-256 6094d0c52c12dcf3fa5d5aede2e59968fe6bc91cd0edd308db4df4553829298d. Part 1 supplies the dated licenseText heading, part 2 the example and nonreplacement passage, and part 3 licenseId, the name “LaTeX Project Public License v1.3c”, the release comment “4 May 2008”, and the cross-references. The record directly supports the release listing while documenting the limits of textual and URL correspondence.

challenge.method: Checked the subject, edition, and digest against all five Index rows. Traced the release tag to the commit serving the SPDX record. Compared the two license headings, both pig.dtx examples, and the full paragraph on nonreplacement derived works. Checked the literal seeAlso URLs and crossRef match fields against the acquisition URL.
challenge.results: Only the 1.3c row matches the claimed subject and publisher digest. The examples disprove verbatim identity. Both name version 1.3 or later in the example grant, but their distribution sentences differ. The publisher example gives copyright 2008, HTTPS, LPPL 1.3c or later, and LaTeX 2008 or later. SPDX gives copyright 2005, HTTP, LPPL 1.3 or later, and LaTeX 2005/12/01 or later. Both full texts contain “Derived Works That Are Not Replacements” and the sentence about clauses 6b and 6d, ruling out a publisher-only reading of the Index note. SPDX cites http://www.latex-project.org/lppl/LPPL-1.3c.txt and https://opensource.org/license/LPPL-1.3c. Its crossRef match values are respectively “false” and “N/A”. Neither entry establishes identity with the captured https://www.latex-project.org/lppl/lppl-1-3c.txt. These differences leave the identifier, edition, and header-date findings intact.

limitations: The Index decision describes a prospective classification for lookup after qualification. It explicitly leaves the discovery disposition unresolved pending protected integration.

The publisher is the original authority for its plaintext. SPDX is the authority for its listing. Its templates, HTML, and repeated comments derive from the same record and supply no independent corroboration of legal equivalence.
The evidence establishes neither locator resolution nor a work-specific grant, redistribution right, installation fact, or legal equivalence.
reasoning: The Index decision records LPPL-1.3c as the discovery identifier for the exact publisher plaintext identified in the claim. The SPDX v3.29.0 tag points to commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, whose detail record declares licenseId LPPL-1.3c. The publisher heading and the SPDX licenseText heading both name LPPL Version 1.3c and give the date 2008-05-04. These facts support the documentary correspondence as of 2026-11-27 America/Chicago.
